query_sentences: Running things is my favourite thing in the world; I chaired our faculty's orientation committee and negotiating with sponsors and getting everyone moving was amazing. I'm also really into keeping things organised, like building schedules, tracking budgets and making sure every detail is in place. Helping freshies settle in was kinda nice too. Hands-on work with tools or machines really isn't for me. I also dislike deep research or theory where you spend hours figuring out why something happens.

I interned at a community centre running programmes for elderly residents and honestly I really liked it, because helping people feel less alone is what I care about most. I'm also curious about why people behave the way they do and read research on it often. Writing and doodling is kinda fun too. What I don't like is routine admin like filing forms and keeping records. Helping people is where I want to be.

I'm not into creative stuff like drawing, writing stories or designing things at all.

I enjoy analysing things and figuring out how they work. I also like tinkering with gadgets and building small projects. Roles where I have to look after or comfort people all day really aren't for me. I'd rather work quietly on a problem. I don't really enjoy analysing things or doing research.

query_diagnostics.provenance_scope: query sources, not attribution of individual retrieved tasks
query_sentences: During my internship last summer I was mostly analysing data and checking results, so maybe it sounds like I only like research because that's what I happened to do. I get quite satisfied when everything is neatly organised and documented. Building or fixing small things can be fun once in a while too. But I don't enjoy having to support or counsel people all day. Persuading people or selling ideas really isn't my thing either.

Nothing satisfies me more than turning a messy spreadsheet into perfect order, with every record checked and every step of the process clearly laid out. I also really like leading a team and persuading people to back a plan, like when our CCA had to convince the school to approve a bigger budget. Working out why the numbers don't add up is genuinely fun for me too. On the other hand, hands-on work with tools, engines or wiring is something I really don't like.

I keep detailed spreadsheets for everything in my own life too. Following clear procedures and getting the details right is what I'm best at. Hands-on physical work like fixing things or building stuff is not for me though.

Being there for people is what matters most to me; I volunteer weekly at a tuition programme for kids from lower-income families and it's the highlight of my week. I'm also really curious about why people behave the way they do, and I like reading studies and testing ideas. Sales pitching or pushing people to buy things isn't really my style. And detailed admin, like updating records and following procedures to the letter, really drains me.

query_sentences: I enjoy analysing things and figuring out how they work. I also like tinkering with gadgets and building small projects. Roles where I have to look after or comfort people all day really aren't for me. I'd rather work quietly on a problem. I don't really enjoy analysing things or doing research.

I'm at my best when I'm leading and persuading; pitching ideas to sponsors and getting a team fired up is what I live for. I'm also really into keeping things orderly, like tracking budgets and planning every detail in a spreadsheet. Helping people out, like guiding juniors through module planning, means a lot to me too. But hands-on stuff with tools, machines or outdoor physical labour I really dislike.

query_sentences: I love working with my hands, building and repairing things is super satisfying. I also enjoy figuring out how things work. My poly lecturers said I was good at facilitating groups and my internship had me running activities for kids, so I've been thinking I should do something about helping people. Being outdoors doing practical stuff is when I feel most alive.

What gets me most excited is digging into a problem and running my own little experiments until I figure out why something happens. I really enjoy fixing things with my hands, like taking apart an old fan and getting it running again. I also like helping my juniors when they're stuck on tutorials. Honestly, I don't really like hands-on, tool-type work at all. I'm not so keen on following a fixed checklist or keeping detailed records, and drawing or designing things isn't really my thing either.

query_sentences: My family has always run its own businesses, so I guess it's natural that I like leading and persuading people, maybe it's just what I've seen growing up. I also like keeping things organised and planned. Creative stuff like drawing or designing really isn't for me. I'm also not keen on roles where I'm mainly caring for people.

I love creating things, whether it's sketching, designing posters for my CCA or writing short stories. I also really enjoy listening to people and helping my friends work through their problems. Reading up on why people behave the way they do is fascinating to me. I actually quite like keeping things organised in spreadsheets and tracking every detail. But I hate fiddly hands-on work with tools, and being outdoors doing physical tasks just drains me. Keeping records and checking every small detail is something I really can't stand.

Since young I've been helping out at my mum's stall at the pasar malam, pitching to customers and handling the bargaining, so people assume I just do sales stuff because it's what I know. I enjoy working with people and helping them feel at ease, and I like creative projects like designing slides or videos for events. Keeping things organised is quite satisfying for me too. I really dislike working with tools or doing physical repairs. Long hours of research and analysing data also bore me badly.
